A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 37 pages, including Appendices A–E. Full text comparison and rendered-page checks establish correspondence of the text, equations, algorithms and figures without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original DP-SGD auditing experiments in Sections 6.2–6.3 and Appendix D.3, plus ORA/AORA simulations for Count-In-Sets in Appendix E.3.2.

after.justification: v4 retains these original DP-SGD experiments and Count-In-Sets simulations, including their reported outcomes in Figures 1–3 and 5–9.

M1.justification: Definition E.3 corrects 'In ORA' to 'In AORA'. This fixes the method name; the adaptive guessing procedure already appears identically in v3's Section 6.3 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: The same DP-SGD gradient-canary scenarios and Count-In-Sets simulations are retained. No dataset, task, domain or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The ORA-versus-AORA comparisons in Figures 3 and 9 retain identical comparator membership. No comparison method is added, removed or revised.

E3.justification: Sections 6.2–6.3 and Appendices D.3/E.3.2 retain the same dimensions, iteration counts, sampling rates, privacy parameters, guesser thresholds and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The analyses varying guess counts, elements per coordinate and privacy levels are unchanged, as are the Xor-in-Pairs and Count-In-Sets demonstrations. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain 200 experiments per point for Figures 1–3, 20 for Figures 7–8 and 100 for Figure 9. Standard-error reporting and the 95% privacy-bound confidence level are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Section 6.2 retains mean epsilon bounds of 0.49 (±0.01) and 0.62 (±0.01) for one and eight elements per coordinate, respectively.

T1.justification: In Proposition E.5's proof, the justification for canceling common 1/2 factors changes from 'Law of total probability' to 'algebra'. This locally corrects a derivation's justification; its equations, assumptions and validity conclusion are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about ORA's three efficacy gaps, tightness characterizations and interference mitigation through multiple canaries and adaptive auditing.

C2.justification: The explanations of interference and adaptivity's benefits are unchanged. Both retain the qualification that the experiments illustrate theoretical insights and leave comprehensive evaluation in realistic settings to future work.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, experimental parameters, guesser specifications, DP-SGD pseudocode and the experiment-code access statement are identical. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 19 references and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning relative to Steinke et al. and contemporaneous work by Xiang et al.

P1.justification: v4 updates the front-page dates/version marking, corrects ORA to AORA in Definition E.3 and edits one proof-step annotation. The remaining wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All nine figures, algorithm displays, captions and page organization are unchanged. Rendered comparisons show 35 pixel-identical pages; differences on pages 1 and 34 are confined to the identified text edits.

improvement.justification: v4 removes a misleading method name in AORA's definition and correctly identifies an algebraic step in its validity proof. These small corrections improve clarity and precision, while the scientific conclusions, empirical support and reproducibility remain unchanged.
